newsitem.title: USA: AmEx finds opening in U.S. bank cards.
newsitem.headline: AmEx finds opening in U.S. bank cards.

text.p: American Express Co pried an opening through the wall around the U.S. bank card business, although its deal with Advanta Corp announced Thursday is short of its objective of forming alliances in which U.S. banks would issue American Express cards.

Advanta, one of the four big U.S. "monoline" card issuers, and a member of both the Visa and MasterCard associations, has launched a new Rewards Accelerator card which will let holders accumulate points in the American Express Membership Rewards program. Advanta is the ninth-largest U.S. card companies based on $12.7 billion in outstanding receivables at the end of the third quarter.

Moshe Orenbuch, an analyst with Sanford C. Bernstein Co, said if the Rewards Accelerator card is successful it could help American Express in its efforts get the Visa and MasterCard U.S. bylaws changed. He said because Advanta now has an exclusive deal with American Express other banks could become more willing to cooperate with American Express if they think they can get something in return.
American Express touts its Membership Rewards program as the best of its kind in the industry.
Orenbuch said the Rewards Acclerator card by itself would not be financially significant to American Express but it could be "somewhat significant to Advanta.

In a telephone press conference, Advanta chief executive officer Alex "Pete' Hart and American Express vice chairman Kenneth Chenault declined to discuss financial arrangments between the two companies. "I'm not going into specifics of this agreement," Hart said.
A press release said the card product was part of a broader alliance between American Express and Advanta.

Hart said the first wave of solicitations for the new cards went into the mail Wednesday night but he declined to say how big the mailing was or how many people the companies expect to sign up for the new card.
Hart also fielded several questions on a U.S. Department of Justice investigation of Visa and Mastercard.
"From everything I understand it's a very active investigation," Hart said.
In Washington, Justice Department spokesman Bill Brooks would only say that any investigation is "ongoing."
American Express has contended bylaws of both the Visa and MasterCard associations, which prevent U.S. members from participating in competing card programs, are anti-competitive.

As for the program announced Thursday by Advanta and American Express, Hart said "it's important to note this is in no way in violation of any aspect of membership in MasterCard or Visa." He said the Advanta alliance with American Express was "totally consistent" with Visa and MasterCard bylaws.

A spokesman for MasterCard said that group would have no comment until it had a chance to review details of the program. Hart, a former executive of MasterCard, said MasterCard chief executive Gene Lockhart was briefed on the announcement in advance.
Visa had no immediate comment.
Chenault was questioned extensively about whether American Express felt business that otherwise went to its Optima charge card would be redirected to the new Rewards Accelerator card.

"We don't believe we're going to lose any business at all," Chenault said. He said while people who transfer balances to the new Rewards accelerator card can earn bonus points, an Optima balance cannot be transferred.
"It leaves Optima in teriffic shape," Chenault said.

Both executives said their objective was to persuade consumers using other bank cards to switch to the new Advanta card. Harvey Golub, American Express chief executive, noted in a statement that the average U.S. consumer uses six separate credit cards.

The Rewards Accelerator card lets holders earn one Membership Rewards point for every $10 of their total month-end balance, including new purchases, cash advances and balance transfers, plus any balance carried over from the previous month.
In order to participate, Rewards Accelerator holders must become or remain American Express card members enrolled in the membership rewards program.
On the American Express cards, one point is earned for every dollar spent.
While it has been battling Visa and MasterCard in the U.S., American Express has had more success in its efforts to partner with banks overseas. On Wednesday, it announced a deal in Spain.
